title: Quiche
notes: Firm and eggy on purpose: 5 eggs for 300 ml of dairy. More milk or cream makes it wobbly and milky.

The pastry: buy all-butter shortcrust (pâte brisée) first. If you only find all-butter puff pastry (pâte feuilletée), use it rather than a shortcrust made without butter; it is flakier but softens sooner.
No onions in this version, on purpose. Add them later if they are missing.
Best warm on the day it is baked; the crust softens in the fridge.

ingredients.name: round sheet of all-butter shortcrust pastry

steps.text: Put a baking tray on a low rack and heat the oven to 170 °C fan.
Line a 26 cm tart tin with {dough}, keeping its baking paper underneath. Prick the base all over with a fork.
Chill, so the pastry holds its shape in the oven.
Meanwhile, put {lardons} in a cold dry pan over medium heat and cook until well browned. Drain on paper towels.
Cover the pastry with baking paper and baking beans. Put the tin on the hot tray and bake until the edges have set.
Lift out the paper and beans. Bake until the base looks dry and golden.
In a bowl, whisk until smooth: {eggs}, {milk}, {cream}, {mustard} and {nutmeg}. Add black pepper but no salt: the lardons and cheese bring enough.
Scatter the lardons over the crust, then half of {cheese}. Pour in the custard and top with the rest of the cheese.
Put the tin back on the hot tray. Bake until golden and set to the centre, 80 °C in the middle on a probe thermometer.
Rest in the tin, so it finishes setting and slices cleanly.
Lift out of the tin, slice and serve warm.
